title: Economic importance of P. falciparum
notes: [Remember] Plasmodium falciparum is the protozoan causing malignant (cerebral) malaria — the deadliest human malaria, transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes; Nepal's Terai is the endemic zone.

[Remember] Life cycle in two hosts: asexual schizogony in humans (liver then red blood cells) and sexual sporogony in mosquitoes; P. falciparum shows accole/several ring forms and crescent (banana-shaped) gametocytes.

[Understand] Harmful importance: high fever with chills, haemolysis and anaemia, cerebral malaria, blackwater fever; resistant strains and drug resistance make it medically the most significant species.

[Understand] Diagnosis and control value: blood-smear study of P. falciparum teaches parasite structure; control — DDT/oil larvicides, bed nets, drainage, chloroquine/artemisinin therapy and surveillance in Terai districts.
[Apply] Table — P. vivax vs P. falciparum (relapse, severity, gametocyte shape, Schüffner's dots absent in falciparum); label the ring stage and gametocyte in a smear sketch.
[Analyze] Why falciparum kills more: heavy parasitaemia, infected-RBC stickiness blocking brain capillaries, rapid drug-resistance development.
[Evaluate/Create] NEB answer frame: define with vector → two-host cycle → symptoms and why malignant → vivax contrast table → Terai control measures.
confusion: Falciparum malaria shows NO relapse from liver hypnozoites (unlike vivax) — do not claim relapse for falciparum.
Crescent (banana-shaped) gametocytes point to falciparum; round gametocytes with Schüffner's dots point to vivax.
'Economic importance' here is mostly harmful (disease burden) plus diagnostic and control value — state both sides.
Mosquito is the vector and second host, not a passive carrier; sporogony happens inside it.

Recall card: vector → cycle → symptom → control.
universalFacts: Falciparum causes malignant tertian malaria with 48-hour fever cycles and possible cerebral blockage.
The crescent gametocyte is the single fastest identification mark in a blood smear.
Terai surveillance plus bed nets and larvicides is the standard Nepal control trio.
examples: Crescent gametocytes in a Terai patient's smear confirming falciparum infection.
Cerebral malaria case from heavy parasitaemia blocking brain capillaries.
Village malaria camp: bed-net distribution plus drain clearing cutting new cases.
